title: Read a notice and spot what is missing
summary: A mail notice tells you when search will be fixed. Who owns the work?
requires: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in a browser with an account that has access.
features: A part of a service can be under repair while another part still works.
roles: Describe which part of an app will change.
prompt: Use only this notice. Make a table with service, start, end, time zone and owner. Put the source words beside each answer. Write unspecified for a fact that is missing.

steps.title: Start with the sample
steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.
steps.help: Copy every heading and row. If Copilot has already answered, you can send the request in your next message.
steps.code: Notice A. Mail search maintenance, Saturday 09:00–09:30 UTC. Message delivery will continue.

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. Notice A gives a 30-minute window, 09:00 to 09:30 UTC. Its owner is unspecified.
steps.help: Put your finger on the start and end times in the notice. Read the sentence about delivery. Search the same notice for any owner before accepting that cell.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Add “Owner: Support Desk” and call it Notice B. Ask for a fresh table.
steps.help: If the table says all mail stops, point to “Message delivery will continue” and ask for a correction.

check: Notice A gives a 30-minute window, 09:00 to 09:30 UTC. Its owner is unspecified.
B names Support Desk. Both notices say delivery will continue.

title: Separate a plan from a firm date
summary: Three messages mention two days. One is booked and one is only an idea.
requires: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in a browser with an account that has access.
features: Someone saying they will check a date has not yet said yes to it.
roles: Find a confirmed mail change window.
Keep proposed game nights off the final schedule.
prompt: List the booked date, proposed date and who owes a reply. Support each answer with a message number. Draft a short question for the approver.

steps.title: Start with the sample
steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.
steps.help: Copy every heading and row. If Copilot has already answered, you can send the request in your next message.
steps.code:
M1 Approver: Tuesday is booked.
M2 Organizer: Could we use Wednesday instead?
M3 Approver: I will check.

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. Tuesday is booked in M1. Wednesday is a request in M2. The approver still owes an answer after M3.
steps.help: Mark booked with a check and could with a question mark. Ask whether the last message resolves the question or simply promises a reply.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Add “M4 Approver: Wednesday is now booked. Cancel Tuesday.” Ask for the list again.
steps.help: If Wednesday appears as booked too soon, ask what word in M3 confirms it. Then read M1 again.

check: Tuesday is booked in M1. Wednesday is a request in M2. The approver still owes an answer after M3.
Wednesday is now booked. Tuesday is canceled. M4 is the key message.
sources: Microsoft · Copilot in each Office app

title: Write a short note for two readers
summary: Users need to know what to do. The help desk needs the same facts in a form it can scan.

features: Different readers can need different words without changing any facts.
roles: Write a release note for players.

steps.title: Start with the sample

steps.code: Build 12. A display bug affects iPad only. Fix rolls out Tuesday 14:00 UTC. Restart the app after rollout. Windows needs no action.

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. Both versions say iPad, Tuesday at 14:00 UTC and restart after the update. Windows needs no action.

steps.help: If the draft gives an Android step, point to the two devices the note names. Ask it to drop extra guesses.

check: Both versions say iPad, Tuesday at 14:00 UTC and restart after the update. Windows needs no action.

title: Read the parts of a meeting you have
summary: A chat starts before the meeting record. Find the decision that someone actually made.
requires: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in a browser with an account that has access.
features: A missing line can change what you can say. Someone asking for nightly exports is not giving approval.
roles: Turn game club notes into a task list.
prompt: Make a short list of approved decisions. Add a source ID, owner and due date if known. Put ideas still waiting for a yes on another line.

steps.title: Start with the sample
steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.
steps.help: Copy every heading and row. If Copilot has already answered, you can send the request in your next message.
steps.code:
09:03 chat C1 Recorder: Could exports run nightly?
09:10 transcript begins
09:12 T1 Approver: I approve weekly exports.
09:13 T2 Recorder: I will own the export job.

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. Weekly exports were approved in T1. The Recorder takes the job in T2. No due date appears.
steps.help: Put T1 beside the decision and T2 beside the owner. Cover T1 with paper. Ask which claim has now lost its support.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Remove T1. Start a fresh chat with just the remaining lines and repeat the request.
steps.help: If the answer calls nightly a decision, ask which line says yes to it.

check: Weekly exports were approved in T1. The Recorder takes the job in T2. No due date appears.
The owner is still visible. There is no longer proof of an approved schedule.

title: Count seats without counting a person twice
summary: One sample account has two plans. A row can also be a repeat.
requires: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in a browser with an account that has access.
features: Counting tickets and counting guests are different jobs. One guest can hold two tickets.
prompt: Count rows, different person-and-plan pairs and different people. List the pairs and people you counted. Keep rows with a missing user separate when counting people.

steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.

steps.code:
Row,Person,Plan
1,u1,A
2,u1,B
3,u2,A
4,u2,A

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. Four rows give three pairs and two people, u1 and u2.
steps.help: Write out u1+A, u1+B and u2+A. Mark the second u2+A as already seen. Compare that list with the four raw rows.

title: Write a slide title the numbers support
summary: A poll went to twelve sites. Nine replied and six said yes. Which share can you claim?
requires: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in a browser with an account that has access.
features: The bottom number of a fraction tells you which group your sentence is about.
roles: Report how many mail tests passed.
prompt: Draft one slide. Give it a short title, both fractions and a speaker note about the missing replies. Label the source Pilot A.

steps.title: Start with the sample
steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.
steps.help: Copy every heading and row. If Copilot has already answered, you can send the request in your next message.
steps.code: Pilot A. Invited: 12 sites. Responded: 9. Respondents supporting extension: 6.

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. Six of nine who replied said yes. Six of twelve invited sites are known to support the idea.
steps.help: Draw twelve dots. Circle the nine replies and color six of those dots. Compare six of the circled dots with six of all twelve.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Ask whether “Two thirds of all pilot sites said yes” fits the data. Give the slide a better title.
steps.help: If a missing reply counts as no, label it unknown instead. Keep the count of actual replies at nine.

check: Six of nine who replied said yes. Six of twelve invited sites are known to support the idea.
A correct title can say “Six of nine replies support the plan.” The other three replies are missing.

title: Sort wait times into four boxes
summary: Build a rule for a mail queue and try the values right at its edges.

features: The time 15 belongs in exactly one box. A missing reading stays missing.
roles: Check age limits on a queue sheet.
Sort game tasks by wait time.
prompt: Below 15 minutes is normal. From 15 through 29 is watch. At 30 and above use investigate. Blank or negative values are invalid. Give each row its label and count each label. Show the rule in words or a formula.

steps.title: Start with the sample
steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.
steps.help: Copy every heading and row. If Copilot has already answered, you can send the request in your next message.
steps.code:
ID,Minutes
A,14
B,15
C,29
D,30
E,
F,-1

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. A is normal, B and C are watch, D is investigate, E and F are invalid.
steps.help: Draw four boxes for the four labels. Place 14 and 15 using the exact edge rule. Put the blank in its own box before doing any math.

title: Pick the rule that was in force
summary: A new rule starts on a certain date. Check the date before checking group size.
requires: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in a browser with an account that has access.
features: Rules work like a dated bus pass. You need the version valid on the day of the trip.
roles: Check which mail move rule applied.
Explain a change in a group policy.
Make old and new game rules work by date.
prompt: Apply V1 before V2 starts. Use V2 starting on its own date. For A through D give held, allowed or unknown. Quote the rule used. Hold groups over the size limit. An unknown flag under V2 means the answer is unknown.

steps.title: Start with the sample
steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.
steps.help: Copy every heading and row. If Copilot has already answered, you can send the request in your next message.
steps.code:
V1 effective Jan 1: groups up to 20 may move.
V2 effective Feb 1: groups up to 30 may move unless flagged; flagged groups are held.
A Jan 31 size 25; B Feb 1 size 30 clear; C Feb 2 size 12 flagged; D Feb 3 size 12 flag unknown.

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. A is held, B allowed, C held and D unknown.
steps.help: Make a tiny calendar with January 31, February 1 and February 2. Write the rule edition over each day and then read its flag rule.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Move the V2 start to February 2. Ask again about B and C.
steps.help: If B stays allowed, compare its February 1 date with the new February 2 start.

check: A is held, B allowed, C held and D unknown.
B now uses V1 and is held. C still uses V2 and is held because of its flag.

title: Build a helper that quotes its rulebook
summary: Two archive rules fit on a card. Ask a helper to stay within them.
requires: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in a browser with an account that has access.
features: Looking up a rule is different from inventing one that sounds fair.
roles: Make a rules helper for a game.
prompt: Use only P1 and P2. Answer three questions. Give the rule number with each answer. Say not covered if neither rule answers. Ask for the request type when it is missing.

steps.title: Start with the sample
steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.
steps.help: Copy every heading and row. If Copilot has already answered, you can send the request in your next message.
steps.code:
P1 Standard archive request: 5 business days.
P2 Urgent archive request: 1 business day.
Q1 Standard archive time? Q2 Restore time? Q3 Archive time?

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. Q1 takes 5 business days under P1. Q2 is not covered. Q3 needs the request type.
steps.help: Look up Q1 in P1. Search P1 and P2 for restore before answering Q2. For Q3, ask which archive rule you should use.

steps.title: Try the second test

steps.help: If the helper gives a restore time, ask which of the two clauses mentions restore.

check: Q1 takes 5 business days under P1. Q2 is not covered. Q3 needs the request type.
The answer is 2 business days and cites P2.

title: Find one rate for two different-sized groups
summary: A big batch and a small one had different results. Work out the rate for all items together.
requires: Open Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in a browser with an account that has access.
features: One batch has four times as many items. Giving the two percentages equal weight answers a different question.
roles: Count game wins across unequal sets of rounds.
prompt: For each batch divide completed by attempted. Add completed items from all batches and divide by all attempts. Also show the simple average of the separate batch rates. Skip a batch with no attempts in that average.

steps.title: Start with the sample
steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.
steps.help: Copy every heading and row. If Copilot has already answered, you can send the request in your next message.
steps.code:
Batch,Attempted,Completed
West,80,72
East,20,10
Idle,0,0

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.

steps.title: Check the first result
steps.text: Compare the result with this hand check. 72/80 is 90%. 10/20 is 50%. Together 82/100 is 82%. The simple average of 90% and 50% is 70%.
steps.help: Add the finished items first, then the attempted items. Divide once. For the other result, write each batch percentage and average those two values.

steps.title: Try the second test
steps.text: Change the small batch to 22 completed out of 20. Ask whether a new final rate is valid.
steps.help: If the total says 70%, ask for the total number finished and total number attempted before dividing.

check: 72/80 is 90%. 10/20 is 50%. Together 82/100 is 82%. The simple average of 90% and 50% is 70%.
The 22/20 row must be fixed. Hold the new rate until the count makes sense.

Microsoft · Copilot in each Office app

title: Put events on one clock
summary: A delay starts before midnight on one clock. Compare times after putting them all in UTC.

Compare scores entered on different clocks.
prompt: Convert dates with known offsets to UTC on one timeline. Label each line with its ID. Work out the minutes from the first delay to recovery. Put unclear times aside. Say what the lines prove about the cause.

steps.title: Start with the sample
steps.text: Open a fresh Copilot chat. Paste the sample below in the message box. You can paste it above the request in the same message.
steps.help: Copy every heading and row. If Copilot has already answered, you can send the request in your next message.

A Jan 5 23:55 -0600: delay observed.
B Jan 6 06:02 +0000: queue peaked.
C Jan 6 01:10 -0500: recovery observed.
D 00:59 offset/date unknown: configuration note.

steps.title: Run the request
steps.text: Send the lab request in the chat holding the sample. Look at its first answer before sending the follow-up.
steps.help: If a new fact appears, ask which part of your short sample supports it. A guess needs a new check.
